newsitem.title: ITALY: Police move in on Venice tower separatists.
newsitem.headline: Police move in on Venice tower separatists.

text.p: Police moved in on Friday to arrest a group of separatists, believed to be armed, who occupied the belltower in St Mark's Square in Venice overnight to call for a separate state in northeast Italy, witnesses said.

Reuters reporter Philip Pullella said he saw at least four members of the group, consisting of about 10 men, being dragged away by armed police. One of the men, dressed in combat fatigues, screamed "Long live St Mark" as he was led away.

Witnesses said the bizarre separatist occupation of the belltower ended after only a few hours when crack Carabinieri paramilitary police commandos scaled the outside of the building using a telescopic ladder. No shots were heard to be fired.
Onlookers cried "Shame" and "You should be thrown in the lagoon" at the separatists as they were dragged off.

The protesters had used what appeared to be a six-wheeled armoured vehicle to crash through the entrance to the 99-metre (325-foot) tower after hijacking a public ferry to reach the square, one of the world's most famous tourist draws.

They had hoisted a banner bearing the symbol of the Lion of St Mark from the top of the tower by the Grand Canal and issued a statement describing themselves a regular unit of the "army" of the "Most Serene Republic of Venice".
